title: What TypeScript is (compared to JavaScript and C#)
intro: TypeScript adds compile-time type checking on top of JavaScript — types erase before any engine runs your code. This module covers how TypeScript differs from JavaScript and C#, the tsc pipeline, tsconfig setup, erasable types, annotations, and gradual JavaScript interop.

overviewDiagram.title: Module overview: from TypeScript source to running JavaScript
overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart TD
  A[Write .ts source] --> B[tsconfig.json rules]
  B --> C[tsc type-check]
  C --> D[Erase types + emit .js]
  D --> E[Optional bundle]
  E --> F[V8 / Browser runs JS]
  G[C# path: IL + CLR] -.->|different host| F

conceptCards.title: TypeScript vs JavaScript vs C#
conceptCards.summary: JS runs in engines. TS checks then erases. C# keeps types in IL metadata enforced by the CLR.
conceptCards.example: JSON.parse in TS is as unsafe at run time as in JS unless you validate.

conceptCards.title: Compile pipeline (tsc)
conceptCards.summary: Parse → type check → transform → emit .js, .d.ts, source maps. Often split: tsc --noEmit + bundler.
conceptCards.example: npx tsc --noEmit in CI; Vite emits for production

conceptCards.title: tsconfig and strict mode
conceptCards.summary: compilerOptions control strictness and emit. Project references scale monorepos with tsc -b.
conceptCards.example: strict: true + module: NodeNext for ESM libraries

conceptCards.title: Erasable types
conceptCards.summary: Interfaces and generics vanish. Classes and enums emit JS. Validate at API boundaries.
conceptCards.example: import type { Order } — erased; class OrderService — emits

conceptCards.title: Annotations and inference
conceptCards.summary: Annotate exports; infer locals. unknown at boundaries, not any.
conceptCards.example: const ids = ['a']; infers string[] — export function needs explicit signature

conceptCards.title: JavaScript interop
conceptCards.summary: allowJs, .d.ts, @types/*, gradual migration. C# ↔ JS is service boundaries, not mixed files.
